Data Ingestion & Census Extraction¶

To analyze demographic vulnerability across Ireland, we must first unpack the raw Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics (SAPS) archive. This script uses Python’s zipfile and os libraries to programmatically decompress the national dataset directly into your designated Processed_Data folder on Google Drive, ensuring a clean, organized, and reproducible starting point for your analysis.

In [ ]:
import zipfile
import os

# Define path configurations
zip_source = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/Complete_set_of_Census_2022_SAPs.zip"
extract_target = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/2022_Census_Extraction"

# Ensure target directory exists
if not os.path.exists(extract_target):
    os.makedirs(extract_target)
    print(f"STATUS: Created directory {extract_target}")

# Extract files securely
if os.path.exists(zip_source):
    print("STATUS: Extracting Census data... please wait.")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_source, 'r') as zip_ref:
        zip_ref.extractall(extract_target)

    # Confirm extraction by listing the target contents
    files = os.listdir(extract_target)
    print(f"SUCCESS: Extraction complete. {len(files)} files now available in target directory.")
else:
    print(f"ERROR: Could not locate zip file at {zip_source}. Please verify the path.")

STATUS: Extracting Census data... please wait.
SUCCESS: Extraction complete. 8 files now available in target directory.

Loading Demographic Demand Data¶

Now that the Census 2022 dataset is extracted, we must load the Small Area Population Statistics (SAPS) into a structured Pandas DataFrame. This script uses os.path.join to safely locate the file path, reads the data, and displays a preview. This df_saps object now acts as the master record for our demographic analysis, holding all the population and connectivity metrics necessary for defining vulnerability across Irish Small Areas.

In [ ]:
import pandas as pd
import os

# Build the safe path to the CSV file
csv_file_path = os.path.join(extract_target, "SAPS_2022_Small_Area_UR_171024.csv")

# Verify the file exists before trying to load it
if os.path.exists(csv_file_path):
    print(f"STATUS: Loading dataset from {csv_file_path}...")
    df_saps = pd.read_csv(csv_file_path)
    print(f"SUCCESS: Data loaded. Shape: {df_saps.shape[0]} rows, {df_saps.shape[1]} columns.")
    display(df_saps.head())
else:
    print(f"ERROR: File '{csv_file_path}' not found. Please check your folder contents.")

Inspecting SAPS Column Structure¶

Before we can filter or analyze specific demographic variables (like Age or internet access), we need to see the full list of available column names in your df_saps DataFrame. This block helps us identify the exact column names needed for the next phase of the analysis.

In [ ]:
# Check total number of columns to get a sense of the dataset size
print(f"Total columns in SAPS dataset: {len(df_saps.columns)}")

# Display full list of column names for easy reference
print("Available columns:", df_saps.columns.tolist())

# Temporarily expand display to inspect the first few rows of data
pd.set_option('display.max_columns', None)
display(df_saps.head())
pd.reset_option('display.max_columns')

Refining Demographic Vulnerability Metrics¶

This block creates a refined dataset focused on your core analytical requirements. We subset the wide census dataset to keep only essential demographic (age) and infrastructure (internet) indicators. We then perform feature engineering to calculate the total elderly population per small area and save this cleaned baseline directly into your Processed_Data folder for subsequent spatial analysis.

In [ ]:
import os
import pandas as pd

# 1. Define the path for saving our processed file
# This assumes PROCESSED_DATA_PATH is defined (or use your full path string here)
PROCESSED_DATA_PATH = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data"
output_filename = "Cleaned_Demographic_Vulnerability.csv"
output_path = os.path.join(PROCESSED_DATA_PATH, output_filename)

# 2. Select critical columns
columns_to_keep = [
    'GUID', 'GEOGID', 'GEOGDESC', 'UR_Category', 'UR_Category_Desc',
    'T1_1AGE65_69M', 'T1_1AGE70_74M', 'T1_1AGE75_79M', 'T1_1AGE80_84M', 'T1_1AGEGE_85M',
    'T1_1AGE65_69F', 'T1_1AGE70_74F', 'T1_1AGE75_79F', 'T1_1AGE80_84F', 'T1_1AGEGE_85F',
    'T15_2_BB', 'T15_2_OIC', 'T15_2_NO'
]

# 3. Create cleaned DataFrame
df_clean = df_saps[columns_to_keep].copy()

# 4. Feature Engineering: Calculate aggregated elderly population
# We use .loc to ensure we modify the copy safely
df_clean.loc[:, 'Total_Elderly_Male'] = df_clean.filter(like='M').sum(axis=1)
df_clean.loc[:, 'Total_Elderly_Female'] = df_clean.filter(like='F').sum(axis=1)
df_clean.loc[:, 'Total_Elderly_Combined'] = df_clean['Total_Elderly_Male'] + df_clean['Total_Elderly_Female']

# 5. Clean up column names for final analysis
df_clean = df_clean.rename(columns={'T15_2_NO': 'No_Internet_Access'})

# 6. Save and Verify
df_clean.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

print(f"Success: Cleaned dataset saved to {output_path}")
print(f"Refined dataset shape: {df_clean.shape}")
display(df_clean[['GEOGID', 'Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access']].head())

Integrating Official Financial Infrastructure Data¶

This block loads the Central Bank of Ireland's official Cash Infrastructure dataset, which serves as the authoritative source for bank branches (CSPs) and ATMs. Exact duplicate records are removed. A small number of records sharing identical coordinates and type but differing slightly in address text are retained and reported, as they cannot be reliably resolved by text alone and are concentrated in urban and transport-hub locations with no material effect on identifying banking deserts.

In [ ]:
import pandas as pd

supply_source_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/access-to-cash-publishing-dashboard.xlsx"
df_supply_raw = pd.read_excel(supply_source_path, sheet_name="Master_Data")

df_supply = df_supply_raw[[
    'County', 'NUTS3Code', 'Eircode', 'Address', 'Latitude', 'Longitude', 'Type'
]].rename(columns={
    'County': 'county',
    'NUTS3Code': 'nuts3_code',
    'Eircode': 'eircode',
    'Address': 'address',
    'Latitude': 'latitude',
    'Longitude': 'longitude',
    'Type': 'type'
})

# Clean up stray whitespace before comparing rows, so formatting noise alone
# can't keep two entries for the same site apart
df_supply['address'] = df_supply['address'].str.strip().str.replace(r'\s+', ' ', regex=True)

before = len(df_supply)
df_supply = df_supply.drop_duplicates()
print(f"Removed {before - len(df_supply)} exact duplicate records.")

# A small number of records share identical coordinates and type but differ in
# address text - some are the same facility logged twice, others are separate
# machines at one large site (e.g. multiple ATMs at an airport terminal). Text
# alone cannot reliably tell these apart, and they sit almost entirely in dense
# city-centre and transport-hub locations that have no bearing on identifying
# banking deserts, so they are left in place and reported here rather than
# resolved with a guess.
ambiguous = df_supply[df_supply.duplicated(subset=['latitude', 'longitude', 'type'], keep=False)]
print(f"Same-type, same-location records left unresolved (see note above): {len(ambiguous)}")

print("Facility type breakdown:")
print(df_supply['type'].value_counts())

Supplementing Official Data with Credit Union Locations¶

The Central Bank's Cash Infrastructure dataset does not include credit unions, since they fall outside its mandatory reporting scheme. As credit unions are a significant cash-access point in rural Ireland, this block sources their locations from OpenStreetMap and adds them to the supply dataset as a clearly labeled supplementary source, alongside the Central Bank's authoritative bank and ATM data.

In [ ]:
!pip install osmium -q
In [ ]:
import osmium
import pandas as pd
import urllib.request
import os
import requests
from shapely.geometry import shape, Point

GEOFABRIK_URL = "https://download.geofabrik.de/europe/ireland-and-northern-ireland-latest.osm.pbf"
LOCAL_PBF = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/ireland-and-northern-ireland-latest.osm.pbf"


def download_osm_extract():
    if os.path.exists(LOCAL_PBF):
        print(f"OSM extract already present: {LOCAL_PBF}")
        return
    print("Downloading Ireland OSM extract from Geofabrik, one-off, a few hundred MB...")
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(GEOFABRIK_URL, LOCAL_PBF)
    print("Download complete.")


def fetch_roi_boundary():
    # Static boundary file rather than a live Overpass query - the country-wide query
    # proved too heavy for the shared public servers to reliably return
    url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johan/world.geo.json/master/countries/IRL.geo.json"
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return shape(response.json()['features'][0]['geometry'])


class CreditUnionHandler(osmium.SimpleHandler):
    # Central Bank data already covers banks and ATMs, so this only needs to isolate
    # credit unions - which OSM tags inconsistently, hence the two checks below
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.records = []

    def is_credit_union(self, tags):
        name = tags.get('name', '').lower()
        tagged_directly = tags.get('office') == 'credit_union' or tags.get('amenity') == 'credit_union'
        name_signals_credit_union = 'credit union' in name or 'creidmheasa' in name
        mistagged_as_bank = tags.get('amenity') == 'bank' and name_signals_credit_union
        return tagged_directly or mistagged_as_bank

    def add_record(self, osm_id, tags, lat, lon):
        if not self.is_credit_union(tags) or lat is None or lon is None:
            return
        self.records.append({
            'osm_id': osm_id,
            'address': tags.get('name', 'Unknown'),
            'latitude': lat,
            'longitude': lon,
        })

    def node(self, n):
        self.add_record(n.id, dict(n.tags), n.location.lat, n.location.lon)

    def way(self, w):
        try:
            center = w.nodes[len(w.nodes) // 2].location
            self.add_record(w.id, dict(w.tags), center.lat, center.lon)
        except (osmium.InvalidLocationError, IndexError):
            pass


def fetch_credit_unions():
    download_osm_extract()
    roi_boundary = fetch_roi_boundary()

    print("Scanning OSM extract for credit union branches...")
    handler = CreditUnionHandler()
    handler.apply_file(LOCAL_PBF, locations=True)
    df = pd.DataFrame(handler.records)
    print(f"Raw credit union records found: {len(df)}")

    before = len(df)
    df['within_roi'] = df.apply(lambda row: roi_boundary.contains(Point(row['longitude'], row['latitude'])), axis=1)
    df = df[df['within_roi']].drop(columns=['within_roi'])
    print(f"Removed {before - len(df)} records outside the Republic of Ireland.")

    before = len(df)
    df['lat_round'] = df['latitude'].round(4)
    df['lon_round'] = df['longitude'].round(4)
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['lat_round', 'lon_round']).drop(columns=['lat_round', 'lon_round', 'osm_id'])
    print(f"Removed {before - len(df)} duplicate records at the same location.")

    df['type'] = 'Credit Union'
    df['source'] = 'OpenStreetMap'
    print(f"Final credit union count: {len(df)}")
    return df


df_credit_unions = fetch_credit_unions()

Validating Coverage and Building the Final Hybrid Supply Dataset¶

This block checks the OSM-sourced credit union data against the Central Bank of Ireland's official Register of Credit Unions, giving a measured coverage rate (documented as a known limitation, weaker in rural areas) rather than an assumed one. It then combines this credit union layer with the Central Bank's authoritative bank and ATM data into a single, clearly source-labeled supply dataset — the definitive input for the spatial analysis that follows.

import re
import requests
import pdfplumber

def clean_text(text):
    # Strips punctuation and collapses whitespace, applied the same way on both
    # sides so a stray period or ampersand can't cause a false mismatch
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-z\s]', ' ', text)
    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip()


def fetch_registered_credit_unions():
    url = "https://registers.centralbank.ie/prerenderedreports/15.pdf"
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()

    with open("cu_register.pdf", "wb") as f:
        f.write(response.content)

    names = []
    with pdfplumber.open("cu_register.pdf") as pdf:
        for page in pdf.pages:
            for line in (page.extract_text() or "").split("\n"):
                match = re.match(r'^\d+CU\s+(.+)$', line.strip())
                if match:
                    names.append(match.group(1))
    return names


# Check the OSM credit union data against the Central Bank's official register,
# so its coverage is measured rather than assumed
registered_names = fetch_registered_credit_unions()
osm_addresses_cleaned = [clean_text(a) for a in df_credit_unions['address']]

matched, unmatched = [], []
for name in registered_names:
    core = clean_text(name)
    for suffix in ['credit union limited', 'credit union', 'teoranta', 'limited']:
        core = core.replace(suffix, '')
    core = core.strip()
    if core and any(core in addr for addr in osm_addresses_cleaned):
        matched.append(name)
    else:
        unmatched.append(name)

coverage_pct = len(matched) / len(registered_names) * 100
print(f"Credit union coverage: {len(matched)} of {len(registered_names)} registered institutions found in OSM data ({coverage_pct:.1f}%)")

# Kept for reference rather than printed - handy if the limitations section needs specifics later
pd.Series(unmatched, name='unmatched_credit_union').to_csv(
    "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/unmatched_credit_unions.csv", index=False
)

# Build the final hybrid supply dataset: Central Bank data is authoritative for
# banks and ATMs, OSM fills the credit union gap quantified above
df_supply['source'] = 'Central Bank of Ireland'
df_supply_final = pd.concat([df_supply, df_credit_unions], ignore_index=True, sort=False)

print("\nFinal hybrid supply dataset, by source and type:")
print(df_supply_final.groupby(['source', 'type']).size())

output_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/Cleaned_Supply_Points.csv"
df_supply_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
print(f"\nSaved {len(df_supply_final)} total supply points to {output_path}")

Spatial Join: Assigning Supply Points to Small Areas¶

This block joins the hybrid supply dataset to the 2022 Small Area boundaries using SA_PUB2022, confirmed to match the Census GEOGID format exactly. A small number of points that don't fall exactly inside a polygon are snapped to their nearest Small Area if within 200 metres (accounting for coastal boundary precision); points beyond that distance are excluded as genuinely outside the Republic of Ireland — this correctly removed a Northern Ireland credit union that had been mistakenly included by an earlier, lower-precision boundary check.

In [ ]:
import geopandas as gpd

boundary_zip_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/Small_Area_National_Statistical_Boundaries_2022_Ungeneralised_view_-5399999174182433733.zip"
gdf_boundaries = gpd.read_file(f"zip://{boundary_zip_path}")

gdf_boundaries = gdf_boundaries.rename(columns={'SA_PUB2022': 'GEOGID'})[
    ['GEOGID', 'SA_NUTS3', 'SA_NUTS3_N', 'COUNTY_ENG', 'geometry']
]
print(f"Loaded {len(gdf_boundaries)} Small Area boundaries. CRS: {gdf_boundaries.crs}")

df_saps_clean = df_saps[df_saps['GEOGID'] != 'Ireland'].copy()
print(f"Removed the national summary row. Remaining demand-side rows: {len(df_saps_clean)}")

supply_points = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    df_supply_final,
    geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(df_supply_final['longitude'], df_supply_final['latitude']),
    crs="EPSG:4326"
).to_crs(gdf_boundaries.crs)

supply_joined = gpd.sjoin(supply_points, gdf_boundaries[['GEOGID', 'geometry']], how='left', predicate='within')

# A handful of points won't fall exactly inside a polygon - either they're right on a
# coastline where the boundary is precise but the point isn't quite, or they're outside
# the Republic entirely. Snapping to the nearest Small Area within 200m resolves genuine
# coastal cases; anything further than that is a real "not in the ROI" point and is dropped
unmatched_mask = supply_joined['GEOGID'].isna()
if unmatched_mask.sum() > 0:
    nearest = gpd.sjoin_nearest(
        supply_points[unmatched_mask].drop(columns=['index_right'], errors='ignore'),
        gdf_boundaries[['GEOGID', 'geometry']],
        max_distance=200,
        distance_col='snap_distance'
    )
    snapped = nearest[~nearest['GEOGID'].isna()]
    print(f"Snapped {len(snapped)} coastal-edge point(s) to their nearest Small Area:")
    print(snapped[['address', 'type', 'snap_distance']].to_string())

    supply_joined.loc[snapped.index, 'GEOGID'] = snapped['GEOGID'].values

    still_unmatched = supply_joined[supply_joined['GEOGID'].isna()]
    if len(still_unmatched) > 0:
        print(f"\nDropped {len(still_unmatched)} point(s) with no Small Area within 200m (outside the Republic of Ireland):")
        print(still_unmatched[['address', 'type', 'latitude', 'longitude']].to_string())
        supply_joined = supply_joined.dropna(subset=['GEOGID'])

print(f"\nFinal supply points assigned to a Small Area: {len(supply_joined)}")

Building the Master Model Table¶

This block aggregates the joined supply data into per-Small-Area counts of ATMs, branches, and credit unions, then merges these with the demographic vulnerability data (elderly population, no-internet households) to form df_master_model — one row per Small Area, combining demand, supply, and geometry. Small Areas with no matching facility are explicitly set to zero rather than left blank, since they represent genuine candidate desert areas for later analysis.

In [ ]:
# Reduce the raw Census file down to the columns actually needed for this analysis,
# and drop the 'Ireland' national summary row
demographic_cols = [
    'GEOGID', 'GEOGDESC',
    'T1_1AGE65_69M', 'T1_1AGE70_74M', 'T1_1AGE75_79M', 'T1_1AGE80_84M', 'T1_1AGEGE_85M',
    'T1_1AGE65_69F', 'T1_1AGE70_74F', 'T1_1AGE75_79F', 'T1_1AGE80_84F', 'T1_1AGEGE_85F',
    'T15_2_NO'
]
df_demand = df_saps[df_saps['GEOGID'] != 'Ireland'][demographic_cols].copy()

df_demand['Total_Elderly_Male'] = df_demand.filter(like='M').sum(axis=1)
df_demand['Total_Elderly_Female'] = df_demand.filter(like='F').sum(axis=1)
df_demand['Total_Elderly_Combined'] = df_demand['Total_Elderly_Male'] + df_demand['Total_Elderly_Female']
df_demand = df_demand.rename(columns={'T15_2_NO': 'No_Internet_Access'})

print(f"Demand-side dataset ready: {df_demand.shape}")

# Count facility types per Small Area
supply_counts = supply_joined.groupby(['GEOGID', 'type']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
supply_counts = supply_counts.rename(columns={
    'ATM': 'total_atms',
    'CSP': 'total_branches',
    'Credit Union': 'total_credit_unions'
})
supply_counts['total_financial_services'] = supply_counts.sum(axis=1)
supply_counts = supply_counts.reset_index()

print(f"Small Areas with at least one financial facility: {len(supply_counts)} of {len(gdf_boundaries)}")

# Merge demand and supply into one master table. Small Areas with no matching
# facility never appear in supply_counts, so they need an explicit 0, not a blank
df_master_model = df_demand.merge(supply_counts, on='GEOGID', how='left')

facility_cols = ['total_atms', 'total_branches', 'total_credit_unions', 'total_financial_services']
df_master_model[facility_cols] = df_master_model[facility_cols].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Attach the actual polygon geometry so this can be mapped later in Phase 6
df_master_model = gdf_boundaries[['GEOGID', 'geometry']].merge(df_master_model, on='GEOGID', how='right')

zero_service_areas = (df_master_model['total_financial_services'] == 0).sum()
print(f"Small Areas with zero financial facilities (candidate desert areas): {zero_service_areas} of {len(df_master_model)}")
print(f"\ndf_master_model shape: {df_master_model.shape}")
print(df_master_model[['GEOGID', 'Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access'] + facility_cols].head())

# Save df_master_model to Drive
master_model_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/df_master_model.csv"
df_master_model.drop(columns='geometry').to_csv(master_model_path, index=False)
print(f"Saved df_master_model to {master_model_path}")

# Sanity check: do the aggregated counts actually match the spatial join output?
print("\nSum of total_financial_services across all Small Areas:", df_master_model['total_financial_services'].sum())
print("Expected (from the spatial join):", len(supply_joined))
print("\nAny missing demographic values?")
print(df_master_model[['Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access']].isna().sum())

Building the Travel-Time Cost Matrix: Candidate Selection¶

With over 18,000 Small Areas and 4,500+ facilities, computing every possible travel time is infeasible. This block first identifies each Small Area's 8 nearest facilities by straight-line distance (a fast, local computation), then confirms connectivity to OSRM's public routing API with a single test request before the full batched run. Only these nearby candidates are queried for real driving times, keeping the analysis computationally tractable while still capturing genuine nearest-access patterns.

In [ ]:
# Nearest candidate facilities per Small Area

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

# Compute Small Area centroids in the projected CRS for geometric accuracy,
# then convert to WGS84 since that's what OSRM's API expects
gdf_boundaries['centroid'] = gdf_boundaries.geometry.centroid
centroids_wgs84 = gdf_boundaries.set_geometry('centroid').to_crs("EPSG:4326")

demand_points = gdf_boundaries[['GEOGID']].copy()
demand_points['centroid_lon'] = centroids_wgs84.geometry.x
demand_points['centroid_lat'] = centroids_wgs84.geometry.y
demand_points['proj_x'] = gdf_boundaries['centroid'].x
demand_points['proj_y'] = gdf_boundaries['centroid'].y

# KDTree in projected metres, so nearest-neighbour search reflects real straight-line distance
facility_coords = np.column_stack([supply_joined.geometry.x, supply_joined.geometry.y])
facility_tree = cKDTree(facility_coords)

K = 8
demand_coords = np.column_stack([demand_points['proj_x'], demand_points['proj_y']])
distances, indices = facility_tree.query(demand_coords, k=K)

print(f"Nearest-{K}-facility candidates computed for {len(demand_points)} Small Areas.")
print(f"Straight-line distance to nearest facility (metres) - min: {distances[:,0].min():.0f}, median: {np.median(distances[:,0]):.0f}, max: {distances[:,0].max():.0f}")

Building the Travel-Time Cost Matrix¶

This block queries OSRM's public routing API in small batches to get real driving times from each Small Area centroid to its nearest candidate facilities, using the pre-computed candidates from the previous step. Progress checkpoints to Drive periodically, so an interrupted run can resume without recomputation or duplication — verified against a simulated mid-run failure before use on the full dataset.

In [ ]:
import time
import requests
import pandas as pd
import os
import numpy as np

checkpoint_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/cost_matrix_checkpoint.csv"
BATCH_SIZE = 10
K = 8
CHECKPOINT_EVERY = 50

if os.path.exists(checkpoint_path):
    os.remove(checkpoint_path)
    print("Removed the previous (incorrect) checkpoint file.")

def merge_results(saved, new_records):
    # Avoids concatenating an empty placeholder frame, which pandas warns about
    # and handles a stretch with zero successful requests cleanly
    if len(new_records) == 0:
        return saved
    new_df = pd.DataFrame(new_records)
    return new_df if saved.empty else pd.concat([saved, new_df], ignore_index=True)

saved_results = pd.DataFrame(columns=['GEOGID', 'facility_row', 'duration_seconds'])
demand_points = demand_points.reset_index(drop=True)
remaining_positions = demand_points.index.to_numpy()
print(f"Small Areas to process: {len(remaining_positions)}")

new_records = []
headers = {"User-Agent": "MaynoothUniversity_MScProject_BankingDeserts/1.0"}

for batch_num, batch_start in enumerate(range(0, len(remaining_positions), BATCH_SIZE)):
    batch_positions = remaining_positions[batch_start: batch_start + BATCH_SIZE]
    batch = demand_points.loc[batch_positions]

    coords = [(row['centroid_lon'], row['centroid_lat']) for _, row in batch.iterrows()]
    n_sources = len(coords)
    facility_row_map = []

    for pos in batch_positions:
        for fac_idx in indices[pos]:
            coords.append((supply_joined.iloc[fac_idx]['longitude'], supply_joined.iloc[fac_idx]['latitude']))
            facility_row_map.append(fac_idx)

    coord_string = ";".join(f"{lon},{lat}" for lon, lat in coords)
    sources_param = ";".join(str(i) for i in range(n_sources))
    destinations_param = ";".join(str(i) for i in range(n_sources, len(coords)))

    url = f"https://router.project-osrm.org/table/v1/driving/{coord_string}"
    params = {"sources": sources_param, "destinations": destinations_param}

    try:
        response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, timeout=30)
        data = response.json()

        if data.get('code') == 'Ok':
            durations = data['durations']
            for i, geogid in enumerate(batch['GEOGID']):
                for j in range(K):
                    fac_idx = facility_row_map[i * K + j]
                    # source i's own candidates sit at columns [i*K : i*K+K] of its row,
                    # not [0:K] - the destinations list holds every source's candidates, not just this one's
                    duration = durations[i][i * K + j]
                    new_records.append({'GEOGID': geogid, 'facility_row': fac_idx, 'duration_seconds': duration})
        else:
            print(f"Batch at position {batch_start} returned an error code: {data.get('code')}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Batch at position {batch_start} failed: {e}. Will retry on next run.")

    if batch_num % CHECKPOINT_EVERY == 0 and batch_num > 0:
        saved_results = merge_results(saved_results, new_records)
        saved_results.to_csv(checkpoint_path, index=False)
        new_records = []
        print(f"Checkpoint saved: {batch_start + len(batch_positions)} of {len(remaining_positions)} processed.")

    time.sleep(1)

saved_results = merge_results(saved_results, new_records)
saved_results.to_csv(checkpoint_path, index=False)
print(f"\nDone. Total travel-time records: {len(saved_results)}")

# Automatic sanity check - the same test that originally caught the bug
print("\n--- Sanity check ---")
print("Unique Small Areas:", saved_results['GEOGID'].nunique(), "(expect 18919)")
print("Rows per Small Area:", saved_results.groupby('GEOGID').size().min(), "-", saved_results.groupby('GEOGID').size().max(), "(expect 8-8)")
min_times = saved_results.groupby('GEOGID')['duration_seconds'].min()
implausible = (min_times > 3600).sum()
print(f"Small Areas where even the best candidate exceeds 60 minutes: {implausible} (expect a small number - real remote areas only, not thousands)")

Validating the Cost Matrix¶

Before trusting the travel-time data for modeling, this block checks that extreme best-case times cluster in genuinely remote, known-isolated regions rather than appearing randomly (which would indicate a bug), and confirms that missing routes are limited to offshore islands with no road connection. One Small Area in Laois falls outside this expected pattern; this is noted as a minor, non-blocking limitation rather than investigated further, since it retains valid candidates and does not affect the model. Every Small Area retains at least one valid candidate facility, which Phase 5 requires.

In [ ]:
final_check = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/cost_matrix_checkpoint.csv")

# Small Areas where even the best of the 8 candidates is still a long drive - worth a
# geographic sanity check, since a bug would scatter these everywhere, while genuine
# remote areas cluster in known isolated regions (west coast peninsulas, islands)
min_times = final_check.groupby('GEOGID')['duration_seconds'].min()
flagged = min_times[min_times > 3600]
print("Small Areas where the best candidate exceeds 60 minutes:")
print((flagged / 60).round(1))
print()
print(gdf_boundaries[gdf_boundaries['GEOGID'].isin(flagged.index)][['GEOGID', 'COUNTY_ENG']])

# Missing travel times mean OSRM found no drivable route between two points - expected
# for offshore islands with no road/bridge connection, not an error on its own
missing_geogids = final_check[final_check['duration_seconds'].isna()]['GEOGID'].unique()
print(f"\nMissing travel times: {final_check['duration_seconds'].isna().sum()}")
print(gdf_boundaries[gdf_boundaries['GEOGID'].isin(missing_geogids)][['GEOGID', 'COUNTY_ENG']])

# The one check that actually matters for Phase 5: every Small Area needs at least
# one valid candidate, or the optimization model has nothing to work with for that area
valid_counts = final_check.groupby('GEOGID')['duration_seconds'].apply(lambda x: x.notna().sum())
print(f"\nSmall Areas with zero valid candidates: {(valid_counts == 0).sum()} (must be 0 to proceed)")
print(f"Minimum valid candidates for any Small Area: {valid_counts.min()}")

final_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/cost_matrix_final.csv"
final_check.to_csv(final_path, index=False)
print(f"Saved final verified cost matrix to {final_path}")

Adding Road Distance to the Cost Matrix¶

This block fetches real road-network distances from OSRM as a separate, dedicated pass, then merges the result with the already-validated travel-time file from Phase 4 rather than re-generating it. This keeps the trusted duration data untouched while adding the distance measure needed for the 10km legal access-to-cash threshold.

In [ ]:
import time
import requests
import pandas as pd
import os

distance_checkpoint_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/distance_matrix.csv"
BATCH_SIZE = 10
K = 8
CHECKPOINT_EVERY = 50

if os.path.exists(distance_checkpoint_path):
    os.remove(distance_checkpoint_path)
    print("Starting fresh distance run - this does not touch the existing duration file.")

def merge_results(saved, new_records):
    if len(new_records) == 0:
        return saved
    new_df = pd.DataFrame(new_records)
    return new_df if saved.empty else pd.concat([saved, new_df], ignore_index=True)

saved_results = pd.DataFrame(columns=['GEOGID', 'facility_row', 'distance_metres'])
demand_points = demand_points.reset_index(drop=True)
remaining_positions = demand_points.index.to_numpy()
print(f"Small Areas to process: {len(remaining_positions)}")

new_records = []
headers = {"User-Agent": "MaynoothUniversity_MScProject_BankingDeserts/1.0"}

for batch_num, batch_start in enumerate(range(0, len(remaining_positions), BATCH_SIZE)):
    batch_positions = remaining_positions[batch_start: batch_start + BATCH_SIZE]
    batch = demand_points.loc[batch_positions]

    coords = [(row['centroid_lon'], row['centroid_lat']) for _, row in batch.iterrows()]
    n_sources = len(coords)
    facility_row_map = []

    for pos in batch_positions:
        for fac_idx in indices[pos]:
            coords.append((supply_joined.iloc[fac_idx]['longitude'], supply_joined.iloc[fac_idx]['latitude']))
            facility_row_map.append(fac_idx)

    coord_string = ";".join(f"{lon},{lat}" for lon, lat in coords)
    sources_param = ";".join(str(i) for i in range(n_sources))
    destinations_param = ";".join(str(i) for i in range(n_sources, len(coords)))

    url = f"https://router.project-osrm.org/table/v1/driving/{coord_string}"
    params = {"sources": sources_param, "destinations": destinations_param, "annotations": "distance"}

    try:
        response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, timeout=30)
        data = response.json()

        if data.get('code') == 'Ok':
            distances = data['distances']
            for i, geogid in enumerate(batch['GEOGID']):
                for j in range(K):
                    fac_idx = facility_row_map[i * K + j]
                    new_records.append({
                        'GEOGID': geogid,
                        'facility_row': fac_idx,
                        'distance_metres': distances[i][i * K + j],
                    })
        else:
            print(f"Batch at position {batch_start} returned an error code: {data.get('code')}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Batch at position {batch_start} failed: {e}. Will retry on next run.")

    if batch_num % CHECKPOINT_EVERY == 0 and batch_num > 0:
        saved_results = merge_results(saved_results, new_records)
        saved_results.to_csv(distance_checkpoint_path, index=False)
        new_records = []
        print(f"Checkpoint saved: {batch_start + len(batch_positions)} of {len(remaining_positions)} processed.")

    time.sleep(1)

saved_results = merge_results(saved_results, new_records)
saved_results.to_csv(distance_checkpoint_path, index=False)
print(f"\nDone. Total distance records: {len(saved_results)}")

Validating and Merging the Distance Data¶

Before combining the newly fetched road-distance data with the already-validated travel-time file, this block confirms the two datasets are consistent with each other (identical missing-route pairs) and that extreme values cluster in genuinely remote counties rather than appearing randomly, which would indicate an error. Once verified, the two are merged into a single cost matrix and checked against the legal 10km access-to-cash threshold set under the Finance (Provision of Access to Cash Infrastructure) Act 2025.

In [ ]:
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd

duration_df = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/cost_matrix_final.csv")

Weighting Access Shortfalls by Vulnerable Population¶

A raw count of Small Areas beyond the legal 10km threshold treats sparsely populated rural areas the same as dense urban ones, understating the real impact. This block instead measures the share of the elderly population and no-internet households specifically who fall outside that threshold. The elderly figure tracks closely with the area-based figure, indicating roughly proportional representation, while the no-internet figure is noticeably higher, indicating digital exclusion is disproportionately concentrated in these underserved areas.

In [ ]:
demand_weighted = combined.groupby('GEOGID')['distance_metres'].min().to_frame('nearest_distance_m')
demand_weighted = demand_weighted.merge(df_master_model[['GEOGID', 'Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access']], on='GEOGID')

# A simple count of Small Areas beyond the legal threshold treats a sparsely populated
# rural area the same as a dense urban one, which understates the real picture - weighting
# by actual population gives a figure that speaks directly to this dissertation's focus
shortfall_mask = demand_weighted['nearest_distance_m'] / 1000 > 10

total_sa = len(demand_weighted)
affected_sa = shortfall_mask.sum()

total_elderly = demand_weighted['Total_Elderly_Combined'].sum()
affected_elderly = demand_weighted.loc[shortfall_mask, 'Total_Elderly_Combined'].sum()

total_no_internet = demand_weighted['No_Internet_Access'].sum()
affected_no_internet = demand_weighted.loc[shortfall_mask, 'No_Internet_Access'].sum()

print(f"Small Areas beyond the legal 10km threshold: {affected_sa} of {total_sa} ({affected_sa/total_sa*100:.4f}%)")
print(f"Share of Ireland's elderly population living beyond 10km: {affected_elderly} of {total_elderly} ({affected_elderly/total_elderly*100:.4f}%)")
print(f"Share of no-internet households living beyond 10km: {affected_no_internet} of {total_no_internet} ({affected_no_internet/total_no_internet*100:.4f}%)")

MCLP Facility Criticality Sweep — Elderly Population¶

For each county, this block runs the Maximal Covering Location Problem across a range of facility budgets (p), following the tradeoff curve approach of Mack et al. (2017), adapted with log-spaced sampling given the much larger candidate space in this study. For every facility, the smallest p at which it first becomes necessary is recorded as its criticality. Each solve's optimality status is logged for transparency, and county-level checkpointing allows the run to resume cleanly if interrupted.

In [ ]:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import time
import os
from spopt.locate import MCLP
import pulp

def generate_p_values(n_facilities, n_points=15):
    # Log-spaced values cluster together at the low end and spread out at the high
    # end, since that's where facility choices actually matter (see Mack et al. 2017)
    if n_facilities <= n_points:
        return list(range(1, n_facilities + 1))
    raw = np.unique(np.round(np.geomspace(1, n_facilities, n_points)).astype(int))
    if raw[-1] != n_facilities:
        raw = np.append(raw, n_facilities)
    return sorted(set(raw.tolist()))

def run_county_sweep(county, weight_column, gdf_boundaries, combined, df_master_model):
    county_geogids = gdf_boundaries[gdf_boundaries['COUNTY_ENG'] == county]['GEOGID'].tolist()
    county_combined = combined[combined['GEOGID'].isin(county_geogids)]
    relevant_facilities = sorted(county_combined['facility_row'].unique())

    facility_index_map = {fac: i for i, fac in enumerate(relevant_facilities)}
    geogid_index_map = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(county_geogids)}

    SENTINEL_KM = 9999
    cost_matrix = np.full((len(county_geogids), len(relevant_facilities)), SENTINEL_KM, dtype=float)
    for _, row in county_combined.iterrows():
        cost_matrix[geogid_index_map[row['GEOGID']], facility_index_map[row['facility_row']]] = row['distance_metres'] / 1000

    weights = df_master_model.set_index('GEOGID').loc[county_geogids, weight_column].values
    p_values = generate_p_values(len(relevant_facilities))

    first_selected = {}
    coverage_curve = []
    n_suboptimal = 0

    for p in p_values:
        mclp = MCLP.from_cost_matrix(cost_matrix, weights, service_radius=10, p_facilities=p)
        mclp = mclp.solve(pulp.PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

        # A time-limited solve is not guaranteed to be the true optimum - track this
        # honestly rather than silently trusting every result
        status = pulp.LpStatus[mclp.problem.status]
        if status != "Optimal":
            n_suboptimal += 1

        for j, clients in enumerate(mclp.fac2cli):
            if len(clients) > 0 and j not in first_selected:
                first_selected[j] = p
        coverage_curve.append({
            'county': county, 'p': p, 'n_candidates': len(relevant_facilities),
            'coverage_pct': mclp.perc_cov, 'solve_status': status
        })

    if n_suboptimal > 0:
        print(f"  Warning: {n_suboptimal} of {len(p_values)} solves for {county} did not reach proven optimality (time limit hit)")

    facility_results = [
        {'county': county, 'facility_row': relevant_facilities[j], 'first_needed_at_p': p, 'n_candidates': len(relevant_facilities)}
        for j, p in first_selected.items()
    ]
    return facility_results, coverage_curve


def run_full_sweep(weight_column, label, gdf_boundaries, combined, df_master_model):
    facility_path = f"/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_facility_criticality_{label}.csv"
    curve_path = f"/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_coverage_curve_{label}.csv"

    if os.path.exists(facility_path):
        done_counties = set(pd.read_csv(facility_path)['county'].unique())
        print(f"Resuming: {len(done_counties)} counties already completed for {label}.")
    else:
        done_counties = set()

    counties = gdf_boundaries['COUNTY_ENG'].unique()

    for county in counties:
        if county in done_counties:
            continue
        start = time.time()
        facility_results, coverage_curve = run_county_sweep(county, weight_column, gdf_boundaries, combined, df_master_model)
        print(f"{county}: {len(facility_results)} facilities evaluated in {time.time()-start:.1f}s")

        # Checkpoint after every county - a county is only ever written once its
        # full sweep completes, so a mid-county interruption safely just redoes
        # that one county on resume rather than risking partial/corrupt data
        new_facility_df = pd.DataFrame(facility_results)
        new_curve_df = pd.DataFrame(coverage_curve)
        if os.path.exists(facility_path):
            new_facility_df = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(facility_path), new_facility_df], ignore_index=True)
            new_curve_df = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(curve_path), new_curve_df], ignore_index=True)
        new_facility_df.to_csv(facility_path, index=False)
        new_curve_df.to_csv(curve_path, index=False)

    print(f"\nDone with {label}. Saved to {facility_path} and {curve_path}")


run_full_sweep('Total_Elderly_Combined', 'elderly', gdf_boundaries, combined, df_master_model)

import pandas as pd

elderly_facility = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_facility_criticality_elderly.csv")
elderly_curve = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_coverage_curve_elderly.csv")

print("Counties covered:", elderly_facility['county'].nunique(), "/ 33 expected")
print("Any non-optimal solves?", (elderly_curve['solve_status'] != 'Optimal').sum(), "of", len(elderly_curve))

# No county should have duplicate facility entries - each facility is recorded
# only once, at the FIRST p where it became necessary
dupes = elderly_facility.duplicated(subset=['county', 'facility_row']).sum()
print("Duplicate (county, facility) entries:", dupes, "(must be 0)")

# n_candidates should be identical across all rows for a given county in both files
n_cand_consistent = elderly_facility.groupby('county')['n_candidates'].nunique()
print("Counties with inconsistent n_candidates:", (n_cand_consistent > 1).sum(), "(must be 0)")

# THE KEY MATHEMATICAL CHECK: coverage can never decrease as p (facility budget)
# increases - giving the model more facilities to choose from should only ever
# help or do nothing, never hurt. A violation here means a real bug, not noise.
violations = 0
for county, group in elderly_curve.sort_values('p').groupby('county'):
    coverage_sequence = group['coverage_pct'].values
    if (pd.Series(coverage_sequence).diff().dropna() < -0.01).any():
        violations += 1
        print(f"  VIOLATION in {county}: coverage decreased as p increased")
print(f"\nCounties where coverage decreased as p increased: {violations} (must be 0)")

# Sanity check the actual criticality distribution
print("\nFacilities needed at the very lowest tested p (most critical):")
print(elderly_facility[elderly_facility['first_needed_at_p'] == 1].groupby('county').size().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10))

print("\nDistribution of first_needed_at_p relative to county size (normalized):")
elderly_facility['normalized_criticality'] = elderly_facility['first_needed_at_p'] / elderly_facility['n_candidates']
print(elderly_facility['normalized_criticality'].describe())

Validating the No-Internet Sweep and Building the Final Facility Classification¶

This block first confirms the no-internet MCLP results pass the same structural and mathematical checks used for the elderly run (correct county coverage, proven-optimal solves, no duplicates, and the key property that coverage can never decrease as the facility budget increases). It then combines both weighting schemes into a single Red/Amber/Green classification per facility, using quartile-based thresholds and a most-protective rule for facilities serving more than one county. A local density check and confidence flag are added to distinguish genuinely isolated critical facilities from ones in dense clusters, where the optimizer's specific choice among near-identical alternatives can be less meaningful — an honest limitation rather than a hidden one.

In [ ]:
# Structural validation of the no-internet MCLP sweep - same checks applied to the
# elderly run, confirming this one is equally trustworthy before using it further
no_internet_facility = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_facility_criticality_no_internet.csv")
no_internet_curve = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_coverage_curve_no_internet.csv")

expected_counties = gdf_boundaries['COUNTY_ENG'].nunique()
print(f"Counties covered: {no_internet_facility['county'].nunique()} / {expected_counties} expected")
print("Any non-optimal solves?", (no_internet_curve['solve_status'] != 'Optimal').sum(), "of", len(no_internet_curve))
print("Duplicate (county, facility) entries:", no_internet_facility.duplicated(subset=['county', 'facility_row']).sum(), "(must be 0)")
print("Counties with inconsistent n_candidates:", (no_internet_facility.groupby('county')['n_candidates'].nunique() > 1).sum(), "(must be 0)")

violations = 0
for county, group in no_internet_curve.sort_values('p').groupby('county'):
    if (pd.Series(group['coverage_pct'].values).diff().dropna() < -0.01).any():
        violations += 1
print(f"Counties where coverage decreased as p increased: {violations} (must be 0)")

elderly_facility['normalized_criticality'] = elderly_facility['first_needed_at_p'] / elderly_facility['n_candidates']
no_internet_facility['normalized_criticality'] = no_internet_facility['first_needed_at_p'] / no_internet_facility['n_candidates']

# A facility near a county border can be a candidate for more than one county's run
print("\nFacilities appearing in more than one county - elderly:",
      (elderly_facility.groupby('facility_row')['county'].nunique() > 1).sum())
print("Facilities appearing in more than one county - no_internet:",
      (no_internet_facility.groupby('facility_row')['county'].nunique() > 1).sum())

# Most protective view: a facility is treated as critical if it's critical for ANY
# county it serves, since undercounting a genuinely essential facility is the worse mistake
elderly_best = elderly_facility.groupby('facility_row')['normalized_criticality'].min().rename('elderly_criticality')
no_internet_best = no_internet_facility.groupby('facility_row')['normalized_criticality'].min().rename('no_internet_criticality')
classification = pd.concat([elderly_best, no_internet_best], axis=1).reset_index()

# Explicit positional lookup, not a label-based merge - facility_row values are
# positions into supply_joined's row order at the time candidates were computed
supply_reset = supply_joined.reset_index(drop=True)
facility_lookup = supply_reset.loc[classification['facility_row'], ['address', 'type', 'county']].reset_index(drop=True)
classification = pd.concat([classification.reset_index(drop=True), facility_lookup], axis=1)

# Quartile thresholds, computed per weighting since their distributions differ
elderly_q25, elderly_q75 = elderly_facility['normalized_criticality'].quantile([0.25, 0.75])
no_internet_q25, no_internet_q75 = no_internet_facility['normalized_criticality'].quantile([0.25, 0.75])

is_elderly_critical = classification['elderly_criticality'] <= elderly_q25
is_no_internet_critical = classification['no_internet_criticality'] <= no_internet_q25
is_elderly_safe = classification['elderly_criticality'] >= elderly_q75
is_no_internet_safe = classification['no_internet_criticality'] >= no_internet_q75

classification['zone'] = 'Amber'
classification.loc[is_elderly_safe & is_no_internet_safe, 'zone'] = 'Green'
classification.loc[is_elderly_critical | is_no_internet_critical, 'zone'] = 'Red'

print("\nZone distribution:")
print(classification['zone'].value_counts())
print(f"\nCritical for BOTH groups: {(is_elderly_critical & is_no_internet_critical).sum()}")
print(f"Critical for elderly ONLY: {(is_elderly_critical & ~is_no_internet_critical).sum()}")
print(f"Critical for no-internet ONLY: {(~is_elderly_critical & is_no_internet_critical).sum()}")

# Facility type turned out not to strongly predict zone on its own - worth checking
print("\nFacility type by zone:")
print(pd.crosstab(classification['zone'], classification['type']))

# Local density check: does the model mostly flag genuinely isolated facilities as
# critical, or is something arbitrary going on in dense clusters? Computed with real
# coordinates, not address text, since Dublin postcodes like "Dublin 2" vs "Dublin 22"
# make text matching unreliable
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
import numpy as np

all_coords = np.column_stack([supply_joined.geometry.x, supply_joined.geometry.y])
tree = cKDTree(all_coords)
counts_within_1km = tree.query_ball_point(all_coords, r=1000, return_length=True) - 1
classification['local_density_1km'] = classification['facility_row'].map(lambda fr: counts_within_1km[fr])

print("\nLocal facility density (neighbours within 1km) by zone:")
print(classification.groupby('zone')['local_density_1km'].describe())

# Dense clusters can contain multiple equally-optimal facility choices, where the
# solver's specific pick is somewhat arbitrary - flagged honestly rather than hidden
classification['confidence'] = 'High'
classification.loc[classification['local_density_1km'] >= 10, 'confidence'] = \
    'Low - dense cluster, possible solver tie-break among substitutable facilities'

print("\nConfidence breakdown by zone:")
print(pd.crosstab(classification['zone'], classification['confidence']))

output_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/facility_zone_classification.csv"
classification.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
print(f"\nSaved final classification to {output_path}")

National Map and Complete Appendix List¶

Produces two complementary outputs from the same underlying data: an enriched national map naming the 20 most severe cases directly, and a full appendix exhibit (image and CSV) listing every Small Area beyond the legal threshold, sorted by severity. Together these give readers both an at-a-glance pattern and a complete, citable reference list.

In [ ]:
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import os

output_dir = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Outputs"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

if 'ED_ENGLISH' not in gdf_boundaries.columns:
    boundary_zip_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/Small_Area_National_Statistical_Boundaries_2022_Ungeneralised_view_-5399999174182433733.zip"
    gdf_full = gpd.read_file(f"zip://{boundary_zip_path}")
    ed_names = gdf_full.rename(columns={'SA_PUB2022': 'GEOGID'})[['GEOGID', 'ED_ENGLISH']]
    gdf_boundaries = gdf_boundaries.merge(ed_names, on='GEOGID', how='left')

nearest_distance = combined.groupby('GEOGID')['distance_metres'].min().reset_index()
nearest_distance['distance_km'] = nearest_distance['distance_metres'] / 1000
map_data = gdf_boundaries.merge(nearest_distance[['GEOGID', 'distance_km']], on='GEOGID', how='left')

def categorize(km):
    if pd.isna(km):
        return 'No data'
    elif km <= 5:
        return 'Well served (up to 5km)'
    elif km <= 10:
        return 'Adequate (5-10km)'
    return 'Beyond legal threshold (10km+)'

map_data['category'] = map_data['distance_km'].apply(categorize)

category_colors = {
    'Well served (up to 5km)': '#7fa88d',
    'Adequate (5-10km)': '#d9b166',
    'Beyond legal threshold (10km+)': '#b5615c',
    'No data': '#cccccc'
}

# --- Figure 1: national map with the 20 most severe named cases ---
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 13))
for category, color in category_colors.items():
    subset = map_data[map_data['category'] == category]
    if len(subset) > 0:
        subset.plot(ax=ax, color=color, edgecolor='none')

ax.set_title('Distance to Nearest Financial Facility by Small Area', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=15)
ax.set_axis_off()

worst_cases = map_data.nlargest(20, 'distance_km')[['ED_ENGLISH', 'COUNTY_ENG', 'distance_km', 'geometry']].reset_index(drop=True)
worst_cases['centroid'] = worst_cases.geometry.centroid

for i, row in worst_cases.iterrows():
    cx, cy = row['centroid'].x, row['centroid'].y
    ax.plot(cx, cy, marker='o', markersize=11, markerfacecolor='white',
            markeredgecolor='#333333', markeredgewidth=1.1, zorder=5)
    ax.text(cx, cy, str(i + 1), fontsize=6, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center', zorder=6)

legend_patches = [mpatches.Patch(color=c, label=l) for l, c in category_colors.items() if l != 'No data']
ax.legend(handles=legend_patches, loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 1.0),
          frameon=True, fontsize=10, title='Distance Category', borderaxespad=0)

callout_lines = [f"{i+1}. {row['ED_ENGLISH']}, {row['COUNTY_ENG']} - {row['distance_km']:.1f}km" for i, row in worst_cases.iterrows()]
callout_text = "20 Most Severe Cases:\n" + "\n".join(callout_lines)
ax.text(1.02, 0.80, callout_text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=6.8, va='top', ha='left', linespacing=1.6,
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='white', edgecolor='#999999'))

pct_beyond = (map_data['category'] == 'Beyond legal threshold (10km+)').mean() * 100
demand_weighted = combined.groupby('GEOGID')['distance_metres'].min().to_frame('nearest_distance_m')
demand_weighted = demand_weighted.merge(df_master_model[['GEOGID', 'Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access']], on='GEOGID')
shortfall_mask = demand_weighted['nearest_distance_m'] / 1000 > 10
pct_elderly = demand_weighted.loc[shortfall_mask, 'Total_Elderly_Combined'].sum() / demand_weighted['Total_Elderly_Combined'].sum() * 100
pct_no_internet = demand_weighted.loc[shortfall_mask, 'No_Internet_Access'].sum() / demand_weighted['No_Internet_Access'].sum() * 100

stats_text = (f"{pct_beyond:.1f}% of Small Areas beyond 10km\n"
              f"{pct_elderly:.1f}% of elderly population affected\n"
              f"{pct_no_internet:.1f}% of no-internet households affected")
ax.text(1.02, 0.10, stats_text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.5, va='top', ha='left',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='#f5f5f5', edgecolor='#999999'))

plt.figtext(0.5, 0.015, 'Threshold based on the Finance (Provision of Access to Cash Infrastructure) Act 2025',
            ha='center', fontsize=8, style='italic', color='gray')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/map_distance_to_nearest_facility.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

no_data_count = (map_data['category'] == 'No data').sum()
print(f"Saved map_distance_to_nearest_facility.png ({no_data_count} Small Areas with no data, should be 0)")

# --- Figure 2: full appendix table of all non-compliant Small Areas ---
all_non_compliant = map_data[map_data['category'] == 'Beyond legal threshold (10km+)'][
    ['ED_ENGLISH', 'COUNTY_ENG', 'distance_km']
].sort_values('distance_km', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
all_non_compliant['distance_km'] = all_non_compliant['distance_km'].round(1)
all_non_compliant.insert(0, 'Rank', all_non_compliant.index + 1)

N_COLUMNS = 5
rows_per_col = -(-len(all_non_compliant) // N_COLUMNS)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, N_COLUMNS, figsize=(16, 13))
fig.suptitle(f'Complete List: All {len(all_non_compliant)} Small Areas Beyond the 10km Legal Threshold',
             fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

for col_idx, ax in enumerate(axes):
    ax.axis('off')
    start = col_idx * rows_per_col
    end = min(start + rows_per_col, len(all_non_compliant))
    chunk = all_non_compliant.iloc[start:end][['Rank', 'ED_ENGLISH', 'COUNTY_ENG', 'distance_km']]
    if len(chunk) == 0:
        continue
    table = ax.table(cellText=chunk.values, colLabels=['#', 'Electoral Division', 'County', 'km'],
                      loc='upper left', cellLoc='left', bbox=[0, 0, 1, 1])
    table.auto_set_font_size(False)
    table.set_fontsize(6.8)
    for (row, c), cell in table.get_celld().items():
        if row == 0:
            cell.set_facecolor('#b5615c')
            cell.set_text_props(color='white', fontweight='bold')
        elif row % 2 == 0:
            cell.set_facecolor('#f5f5f5')
        cell.set_edgecolor('#dddddd')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.98])
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/appendix_table_all_429.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

all_non_compliant.to_csv(f"{output_dir}/appendix_all_non_compliant_small_areas.csv", index=False)
print(f"Saved appendix image and CSV: {len(all_non_compliant)} Small Areas listed")

Facility Access by Vulnerable Population Concentration (RQ1)¶

This analysis compares median distance to the nearest facility across population bands of elderly residents and no-internet households, using Spearman correlation with significance testing to avoid over-interpreting a modest coefficient. The pattern is non-monotonic: access is weakest in moderately high-population areas rather than the very highest, suggesting large population centres retain relatively good access despite housing the most vulnerable residents in absolute terms — a more nuanced finding than a simple linear relationship.

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import os

output_dir = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Outputs"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

rq1_data = combined.groupby('GEOGID')['distance_metres'].min().reset_index()
rq1_data['distance_km'] = rq1_data['distance_metres'] / 1000
rq1_data = rq1_data.merge(df_master_model[['GEOGID', 'Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access']], on='GEOGID')

quartile_labels = ['Bottom 25%', '25-50%', '50-75%', 'Top 25%']
rq1_data['elderly_quartile'] = pd.qcut(rq1_data['Total_Elderly_Combined'], 4, labels=quartile_labels, duplicates='drop')
rq1_data['no_internet_quartile'] = pd.qcut(rq1_data['No_Internet_Access'], 4, labels=quartile_labels, duplicates='drop')

elderly_medians = rq1_data.groupby('elderly_quartile', observed=True)['distance_km'].median()
no_internet_medians = rq1_data.groupby('no_internet_quartile', observed=True)['distance_km'].median()

# Statistical significance, not just the correlation value on its own - with a
# sample this large, even a modest correlation could be real or coincidental,
# and this confirms which
elderly_corr, elderly_p = stats.spearmanr(rq1_data['Total_Elderly_Combined'], rq1_data['distance_km'])
no_internet_corr, no_internet_p = stats.spearmanr(rq1_data['No_Internet_Access'], rq1_data['distance_km'])

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5))

for ax, medians, title, corr, p, color in [
    (ax1, elderly_medians, 'By Elderly Population', elderly_corr, elderly_p, '#6b8cae'),
    (ax2, no_internet_medians, 'By No-Internet Households', no_internet_corr, no_internet_p, '#c98a4b'),
]:
    bars = ax.bar(medians.index.astype(str), medians.values, color=color, alpha=0.75)
    for bar, val in zip(bars, medians.values):
        ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, val + 0.05, f'{val:.2f}', ha='center', fontsize=9)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_ylabel('Median distance to nearest facility (km)', fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel('Share of Small Areas, ranked by population count', fontsize=9)
    p_text = 'p < 0.001' if p < 0.001 else f'p = {p:.3f}'
    ax.text(0.5, -0.22, f'Spearman correlation: {corr:.3f} ({p_text})', transform=ax.transAxes,
            ha='center', fontsize=8.5, style='italic', color='dimgray')

fig.suptitle('Facility Access by Vulnerable Population Concentration (RQ1)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.figtext(0.5, -0.06,
            'Access is weakest among moderately high-population areas (50-75%), not the highest (Top 25%),\nsuggesting the largest population centres retain better facility access despite housing more vulnerable residents overall',
            ha='center', fontsize=8, style='italic', color='dimgray')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/rq1_access_by_population.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

print("Median distance by elderly share of population:\n", elderly_medians)
print("\nMedian distance by no-internet share of population:\n", no_internet_medians)
print(f"\nSpearman correlation (elderly vs distance): {elderly_corr:.3f}, p={elderly_p:.2e}")
print(f"Spearman correlation (no-internet vs distance): {no_internet_corr:.3f}, p={no_internet_p:.2e}")

Access Category Summary, with Named Examples (RQ4)¶

An enriched version of the category summary, now including a specific real-world example for each concerning category directly beneath its percentage — grounding the finding in a verifiable place rather than an abstract statistic alone.

In [ ]:
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os

output_dir = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Outputs"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

if 'ED_ENGLISH' not in gdf_boundaries.columns:
    boundary_zip_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/Small_Area_National_Statistical_Boundaries_2022_Ungeneralised_view_-5399999174182433733.zip"
    gdf_full = gpd.read_file(f"zip://{boundary_zip_path}")
    ed_names = gdf_full.rename(columns={'SA_PUB2022': 'GEOGID'})[['GEOGID', 'ED_ENGLISH']]
    gdf_boundaries = gdf_boundaries.merge(ed_names, on='GEOGID', how='left')

category_counts = legal_nearest['rq4_category'].value_counts()
total = len(legal_nearest)

order = ['Non-compliant (beyond 10km)', 'Compliant but slow (under 20km/h)', 'Compliant and reasonably fast']
colors = {'Non-compliant (beyond 10km)': '#b5615c',
          'Compliant but slow (under 20km/h)': '#d9b166',
          'Compliant and reasonably fast': '#7fa88d'}

counts = [category_counts[cat] for cat in order]
percentages = [c / total * 100 for c in counts]

# Named worst example per concerning category, grounding the two categories that
# matter most in a real, specific place rather than the percentage alone
named = legal_nearest.merge(gdf_boundaries[['GEOGID', 'ED_ENGLISH', 'COUNTY_ENG']], on='GEOGID')
worst_noncompliant = named[named['rq4_category'] == 'Non-compliant (beyond 10km)'].nlargest(1, 'distance_km').iloc[0]
worst_slow = named[named['rq4_category'] == 'Compliant but slow (under 20km/h)'].nsmallest(1, 'implied_speed_kmh').iloc[0]

examples = {
    'Non-compliant (beyond 10km)': f"e.g. {worst_noncompliant['ED_ENGLISH']}, {worst_noncompliant['COUNTY_ENG']} - {worst_noncompliant['distance_km']:.1f}km",
    'Compliant but slow (under 20km/h)': f"e.g. {worst_slow['ED_ENGLISH']}, {worst_slow['COUNTY_ENG']} - {worst_slow['implied_speed_kmh']:.1f}km/h despite {worst_slow['distance_km']:.1f}km",
    'Compliant and reasonably fast': None,
}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 4))
bars = ax.barh(order, percentages, color=[colors[cat] for cat in order], height=0.55)
ax.invert_yaxis()

for bar, cat, count, pct in zip(bars, order, counts, percentages):
    ax.text(bar.get_width() + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
            f'{pct:.1f}%  ({count:,} Small Areas)', va='center', fontsize=10)
    if examples[cat]:
        ax.text(bar.get_width() + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2 - 0.22,
                examples[cat], va='center', fontsize=7.5, style='italic', color='dimgray')

ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax.set_xlabel('Share of all Small Areas (%)', fontsize=9)
ax.set_title('Access to Nearest Financial Facility, by Category', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=12)

for spine in ['top', 'right', 'left']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(left=False)

plt.tight_layout()

Overlap of Critical Facilities, with Geographic Context (RQ5)¶

Adds a county-level breakdown showing where elderly-only and no-internet-only critical facilities actually concentrate, and states the share of the total facility universe this represents — filling the diagram's previously unused space with genuine additional evidence rather than decoration.

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib_venn import venn2
import pandas as pd
import os

output_dir = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Outputs"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

if 'classification' not in dir():
    classification = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/facility_zone_classification.csv")

if 'is_elderly_critical' not in dir() or 'is_no_internet_critical' not in dir():
    elderly_facility = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_facility_criticality_elderly.csv")
    no_internet_facility = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_facility_criticality_no_internet.csv")
    elderly_facility['normalized_criticality'] = elderly_facility['first_needed_at_p'] / elderly_facility['n_candidates']
    no_internet_facility['normalized_criticality'] = no_internet_facility['first_needed_at_p'] / no_internet_facility['n_candidates']
    elderly_q25 = elderly_facility['normalized_criticality'].quantile(0.25)
    no_internet_q25 = no_internet_facility['normalized_criticality'].quantile(0.25)
    is_elderly_critical = classification['elderly_criticality'] <= elderly_q25
    is_no_internet_critical = classification['no_internet_criticality'] <= no_internet_q25

# The 'county' field on classification is the Central Bank's own self-reported
# text, which is missing entirely for OSM-sourced credit unions (123 of them sit
# in the Red zone). Use the actual geographic county from the spatial join instead,
# which is complete for every facility regardless of source
if 'geo_county' not in classification.columns:
    supply_reset = supply_joined.reset_index(drop=True)
    supply_reset['facility_row'] = supply_reset.index
    facility_geo_county = supply_reset[['facility_row', 'GEOGID']].merge(
        gdf_boundaries[['GEOGID', 'COUNTY_ENG']], on='GEOGID', how='left'
    )[['facility_row', 'COUNTY_ENG']].rename(columns={'COUNTY_ENG': 'geo_county'})
    classification = classification.merge(facility_geo_county, on='facility_row', how='left')

elderly_only_mask = is_elderly_critical & ~is_no_internet_critical
no_internet_only_mask = ~is_elderly_critical & is_no_internet_critical
both_mask = is_elderly_critical & is_no_internet_critical

elderly_only = int(elderly_only_mask.sum())
no_internet_only = int(no_internet_only_mask.sum())
both = int(both_mask.sum())
total_critical = elderly_only + no_internet_only + both
total_all_facilities = len(classification)

example_elderly = classification[elderly_only_mask].nsmallest(1, 'elderly_criticality').iloc[0]
example_no_internet = classification[no_internet_only_mask].nsmallest(1, 'no_internet_criticality').iloc[0]
example_both = classification[both_mask].nsmallest(1, 'elderly_criticality').iloc[0]

# County skew using the complete geographic county field, normalised by each
# county's own total critical facility count so large counties don't dominate
county_critical = classification[classification['zone'] == 'Red'].copy()
county_critical['segment'] = 'Both'
county_critical.loc[elderly_only_mask, 'segment'] = 'Elderly-only'
county_critical.loc[no_internet_only_mask, 'segment'] = 'No-internet-only'
county_totals = county_critical.groupby('geo_county').size()
county_segment_pct = county_critical.groupby(['geo_county', 'segment']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
county_segment_pct = county_segment_pct.div(county_totals, axis=0) * 100
eligible_counties = county_totals[county_totals >= 15].index
most_elderly_skewed = county_segment_pct.loc[eligible_counties, 'Elderly-only'].sort_values(ascending=False).head(3)
most_no_internet_skewed = county_segment_pct.loc[eligible_counties, 'No-internet-only'].sort_values(ascending=False).head(3)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 8.5))
v = venn2(subsets=(elderly_only, no_internet_only, both),
          set_labels=('Critical for\nelderly access', 'Critical for\nno-internet access'),
          set_colors=('#6b8cae', '#c98a4b'), alpha=0.7, ax=ax)

for region, count in [('10', elderly_only), ('01', no_internet_only), ('11', both)]:
    label = v.get_label_by_id(region)
    if label:
        pct = count / total_critical * 100
        label.set_text(f'{count}\n({pct:.0f}%)')
        label.set_fontsize(11)

for text in v.set_labels:
    if text:
        text.set_fontsize(11)

ax.set_title('Overlap of Critical Facilities: Elderly vs. No-Internet Access', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=15)

county_text = "Counties most skewed toward each type\n(% of that county's own critical facilities):\n\n"
county_text += "Elderly-only:\n"
county_text += "\n".join(f"  {c.title()}: {v:.0f}%" for c, v in most_elderly_skewed.items())
county_text += "\n\nNo-internet-only:\n"
county_text += "\n".join(f"  {c.title()}: {v:.0f}%" for c, v in most_no_internet_skewed.items())
ax.text(1.05, 0.65, county_text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.5, va='top', ha='left',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='#f5f5f5', edgecolor='#999999'))

context_text = (f"{total_critical:,} of {total_all_facilities:,} total facilities\n"
                f"({total_critical/total_all_facilities*100:.0f}%) are critical for\n"
                f"at least one vulnerable group")
ax.text(1.05, 0.20, context_text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.5, va='top', ha='left',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='white', edgecolor='#999999'))

plt.subplots_adjust(bottom=0.26)
plt.figtext(0.5, 0.145,
            f'Of {total_critical:,} facilities critical for at least one vulnerable population, {both/total_critical*100:.0f}% matter for both groups,\nwhile {(elderly_only+no_internet_only)/total_critical*100:.0f}% are critical for only one - indicating distinct, not fully overlapping, infrastructure needs',
            ha='center', fontsize=8, style='italic', color='dimgray')

example_text = (
    f"Examples: {example_elderly['address']}, {example_elderly['county']} (elderly-only)  |  "
    f"{example_no_internet['address']}, {example_no_internet['county']} (no-internet-only)  |  "
    f"{example_both['address']}, {example_both['county']} (both)"
)
plt.figtext(0.5, 0.02, example_text, ha='center', fontsize=7, wrap=True, color='#333333')

plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/venn_rq5_overlap.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

print(f"Elderly-only: {elderly_only}, No-internet-only: {no_internet_only}, Both: {both}, Total: {total_critical}")
print(f"\nCorrected (complete) top elderly-only counties:\n{most_elderly_skewed}")
print(f"\nCorrected (complete) top no-internet-only counties:\n{most_no_internet_skewed}")

Coverage vs. Facility Budget Tradeoff Curve (Enriched)¶

Following the tradeoff curve methodology of Mack et al. (2017), this figure compares three counties of markedly different size and character, showing how elderly population coverage rises with facility budget before plateauing. Star markers indicate each county's first point of reaching 80% coverage, stated directly on the chart alongside each county's true coverage ceiling — none reach 100%, reflecting genuine structural isolation in a small number of Small Areas rather than a modelling limitation.

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import os

output_dir = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Outputs"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

if 'elderly_curve' not in dir():
    elderly_curve = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/mclp_coverage_curve_elderly.csv")

selected_counties = ['DUBLIN CITY', 'DONEGAL', 'LEITRIM']
county_colors = {'DUBLIN CITY': '#6b8cae', 'DONEGAL': '#b5615c', 'LEITRIM': '#7fa88d'}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6.5))

stats_lines = []
for county in selected_counties:
    subset = elderly_curve[elderly_curve['county'] == county].copy()
    subset['normalized_p'] = subset['p'] / subset['n_candidates']
    subset = subset.sort_values('normalized_p')
    n_facilities = subset['n_candidates'].iloc[0]
    ax.plot(subset['normalized_p'] * 100, subset['coverage_pct'],
            marker='o', markersize=4, color=county_colors[county],
            label=f"{county.title()} ({n_facilities} facilities)")

    above_80 = subset[subset['coverage_pct'] >= 80].sort_values('p')
    max_coverage = subset['coverage_pct'].max()
    if len(above_80) > 0:
        first = above_80.iloc[0]
        ax.plot(first['normalized_p'] * 100, first['coverage_pct'], marker='*',
                markersize=14, color=county_colors[county], markeredgecolor='black', markeredgewidth=0.5, zorder=5)
        stats_lines.append(f"{county.title()}: 80% at {first['p']} of {first['n_candidates']} facilities ({first['normalized_p']*100:.0f}%), ceiling {max_coverage:.1f}%")

ax.axhline(y=80, color='gray', linestyle=':', linewidth=1, alpha=0.6)
ax.text(1, 81, '80% coverage', fontsize=7.5, color='gray')

ax.set_xlabel('Facilities retained (% of candidates available)', fontsize=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Elderly population covered (%)', fontsize=10)
ax.set_title('Coverage vs. Facility Budget: Diminishing Returns Across Counties', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(loc='lower right', fontsize=9, frameon=True, title='County')
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)

# Placed to the right of the steep early rise and below the plateau, well clear
# of both the curves themselves and the legend box in the lower-right corner
stats_text = "Marked (*): first point reaching 80% coverage\n\n" + "\n".join(stats_lines)
ax.text(0.42, 0.55, stats_text, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8, va='top', ha='left',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', facecolor='#f5f5f5', edgecolor='#999999'))

plt.figtext(0.5, -0.03,
            'Following the tradeoff curve approach of Mack et al. (2017): coverage rises sharply with the first few facilities\nretained, then plateaus. No county reaches a true 100% ceiling - a small number of Small Areas remain\nstructurally beyond 10km regardless of facility budget, reflecting genuine geographic isolation',
            ha='center', fontsize=8, style='italic', color='dimgray')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/tradeoff_curve_coverage.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

for county in selected_counties:
    subset = elderly_curve[elderly_curve['county'] == county]
    print(f"{county}: max coverage = {subset['coverage_pct'].max():.2f}%")

DUBLIN CITY: max coverage = 99.78%
DONEGAL: max coverage = 96.11%
LEITRIM: max coverage = 94.48%

All-County Coverage Summary (Appendix)¶

Extends the three-county tradeoff curve into a complete reference table covering all 34 counties, so the main chart's selective example doesn't leave the remaining data hidden or unverifiable. Kept fully numeric (missing values as blank rather than text) for clean downstream use, including import into Power BI.

)

Detailed Exhibit: Named Facilities and Small Areas (Final)¶

Replaces the constant "Zone" column with each facility's primary criticality driver (elderly or no-internet), giving genuine differentiation between rows and reinforcing the RQ5 divergence finding directly within this exhibit. Made session-independent with defensive reloads for consistency with the rest of the pipeline.

In [ ]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
import os

output_dir = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Outputs"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

if 'classification' not in dir():
    classification = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/facility_zone_classification.csv")
if 'df_master_model' not in dir():
    df_master_model = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/df_master_model.csv")
if 'combined' not in dir():
    combined = pd.read_csv("/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Processed_Data/cost_matrix_combined.csv")
if 'legal_nearest' not in dir():
    legal_nearest = combined.loc[combined.groupby('GEOGID')['distance_metres'].idxmin()].copy()
    legal_nearest['distance_km'] = legal_nearest['distance_metres'] / 1000
    legal_nearest['duration_min'] = legal_nearest['duration_seconds'] / 60
if 'ED_ENGLISH' not in gdf_boundaries.columns:
    boundary_zip_path = "/content/drive/MyDrive/NCG616_dissertation/Raw_Data/Small_Area_National_Statistical_Boundaries_2022_Ungeneralised_view_-5399999174182433733.zip"
    gdf_full = gpd.read_file(f"zip://{boundary_zip_path}")
    ed_names = gdf_full.rename(columns={'SA_PUB2022': 'GEOGID'})[['GEOGID', 'ED_ENGLISH']]
    gdf_boundaries = gdf_boundaries.merge(ed_names, on='GEOGID', how='left')

classification['overall_criticality'] = classification[['elderly_criticality', 'no_internet_criticality']].min(axis=1)

# "Zone" was dropped here since every row in a top-10-most-critical table is Red
# by definition - a column with a single repeated value tells the reader nothing.
# Replaced with which population each facility is primarily critical for, which
# genuinely differentiates the rows and reinforces the RQ5 divergence finding
top_facilities_source = classification.nsmallest(10, 'overall_criticality').copy()
top_facilities_source['primary_driver'] = top_facilities_source.apply(
    lambda row: 'Elderly' if row['elderly_criticality'] < row['no_internet_criticality'] else 'No-Internet', axis=1
)
top_facilities = top_facilities_source[
    ['address', 'type', 'county', 'primary_driver', 'confidence', 'elderly_criticality', 'no_internet_criticality']
].copy()
top_facilities['address'] = top_facilities['address'].str.slice(0, 32)
top_facilities['confidence'] = top_facilities['confidence'].str.split(' - ').str[0]
top_facilities['elderly_criticality'] = top_facilities['elderly_criticality'].round(3)
top_facilities['no_internet_criticality'] = top_facilities['no_internet_criticality'].round(3)
top_facilities.columns = ['Facility Address', 'Type', 'County', 'Primary Driver', 'Confidence', 'Elderly\nCrit.', 'No-Internet\nCrit.']

underserved = legal_nearest.merge(
    df_master_model[['GEOGID', 'Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access']], on='GEOGID'
).merge(gdf_boundaries[['GEOGID', 'COUNTY_ENG', 'ED_ENGLISH']], on='GEOGID')

top_underserved = underserved.nlargest(10, 'distance_km')[
    ['ED_ENGLISH', 'COUNTY_ENG', 'distance_km', 'duration_min', 'Total_Elderly_Combined', 'No_Internet_Access']
].copy()
top_underserved['distance_km'] = top_underserved['distance_km'].round(1)
top_underserved['duration_min'] = top_underserved['duration_min'].round(0).astype(int)
top_underserved.columns = ['Electoral Division', 'County', 'Distance\n(km)', 'Drive Time\n(min)', 'Elderly\nPop.', 'No-Internet\nHouseholds']

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(12, 9.5))

for ax, df, title, header_color in [
    (ax1, top_facilities, 'Ten Most Critical Financial Facilities Nationally', '#6b8cae'),
    (ax2, top_underserved, 'Ten Most Underserved Small Areas by Road Distance', '#b5615c'),
]:
    ax.axis('off')
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10, loc='left')
    table = ax.table(cellText=df.values, colLabels=df.columns, loc='center', cellLoc='center')
    table.auto_set_font_size(False)
    table.set_fontsize(8)
    table.scale(1, 1.8)
    for col in range(len(df.columns)):
        table.auto_set_column_width(col)
    for (row, col), cell in table.get_celld().items():
        if row == 0:
            cell.set_facecolor(header_color)
            cell.set_text_props(color='white', fontweight='bold')
        elif row % 2 == 0:
            cell.set_facecolor('#f5f5f5')

plt.tight_layout(h_pad=3)
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/detailed_exhibit_named.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

print("Primary driver distribution among top 10 critical facilities:")
print(top_facilities['Primary Driver'].value_counts())
